title: Shifted global Hom cohomology and site hypercohomology comparison
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $P,Q$ objects of $D(O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. For all integers $m,n$ there are additive equivalences $c:H^{n-m}(R\Gamma(X,RHom(P,Q)))\simeq H^0(X,RHom(P[m],Q[n]))$, between the underlying global module cohomology group [def-pc-global-derived-rhom] and site hypercohomology [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For every $q:Q\to Q\prime$ and class $x$, $c_{P,Q\prime,m,n}(H^{n-m}(R\Gamma RHom(P,q))(x))=H^0(X,RHom(id_{P[m]},q[n]))(c_{P,Q,m,n}(x))$. No boundedness or quasi-coherence is assumed; sheaf and module localization universes are independent.

source.place: Tag 08JA, proof of Lemma 21.35.1; cohomology.tex Tag 0B6A, Section 20.44

proof.text: Choose a K-flat representative L of P and a K-injective representative I of Q. Compute internal Hom by Hom(L,I), independent of choices, using the internal-Hom representative comparison and quasi-isomorphism invariance. The Hom complex is K-injective and hence termwise global sections compute derived global sections.

Shifts preserve K-flatness and K-injectivity by shifting the acyclic test complex in the defining conditions. In degree k, reindex Hom(L[m],I[n]) from p to p+m and multiply by (-1)^(m*k), identifying it with Hom(L,I)[n-m]. The differentials differ before multiplication by (-1)^m; the adjacent-degree factors rectify this. Thus H^0 of shifted global Hom is H^(n-m) of unshifted global Hom, naturally in the second argument.

Evaluation at 1 gives an additive isomorphism between the underlying group of global sections and Hom_O(O,-); its inverse sends s to multiplication by s. These commute with differentials and sheaf maps. Compute both right derived functors on the K-injective Hom complex and take cohomology. Transport through resolution comparisons; all maps commute with shifted representative morphisms, giving the asserted naturality for derived q.

theorem schemeGlobalHom_shiftedHypercohomology_equiv
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (R : Type u) [Ring R], HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ c : ∀ (P Q : schemeDerivedCategory X) (m n : ℤ),
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) (n - m)).obj
          ((schemeGlobalDerivedHom X).obj (op P, Q))) ≃+
        ((ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) X.sheaf).obj
          ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) X.sheaf).obj
            (op (P⟦m⟧), Q⟦n⟧))),
      ∀ (P Q Q' : schemeDerivedCategory X) (m n : ℤ) (q : Q ⟶ Q')
        (x : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) (n - m)).obj
            ((schemeGlobalDerivedHom X).obj (op P, Q)))),
        c P Q' m n
          (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) (n - m)).map
              ((schemeGlobalDerivedHom X).map ((𝟙 P).op, q))) x) =
          (ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) X.sheaf).map
            ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) X.sheaf).map
              ((𝟙 (P⟦m⟧)).op, q⟦n⟧')) (c P Q m n x)
